name: Inbound email parsing
needs: let users reply to a notification email and have it show up in the app
forward receipts to a special address
create a ticket when someone emails support
each user gets their own email address in my app
summary: Letting your app receive email. A provider accepts mail for an address or domain you own, turns each message into JSON (sender, subject, text, attachments) and posts it to a webhook in your app.
need_when: Users should reply to notifications by email, forward things in, or email a unique address to add data.
skip_when: You only need to read one mailbox occasionally. A shared inbox tool may be enough.

ways.title: Your email provider's inbound webhook
ways.how: Postmark, SendGrid Inbound Parse, Mailgun Routes, Resend and Amazon SES receiving post parsed messages to your URL.
ways.tradeoff: Reliable and simple. You point a subdomain's MX record at them.

ways.title: Cloudflare Email Routing with a Worker
ways.how: Email Workers receive messages for your domain and can forward or post them to your app.
ways.tradeoff: Free and flexible. You parse MIME yourself (postal-mime helps).

ways.title: Poll a mailbox over IMAP
ways.how: A scheduled job reads a dedicated mailbox and processes new messages.
ways.tradeoff: Works with any mailbox. Slower, and fragile with folder states and logins.

prompt:
Let my app receive email at [reply.mydomain.com] using [provider]'s inbound webhook.

Requirements:
- Use a subdomain for MX so normal company mail is unaffected.
- Verify each webhook is from the provider (signature, basic auth or secret path) and store the raw message id so retries aren't processed twice.
- Route by address: reply+<token>@ maps to a thread with a random token, not a guessable id.
- Check the sender matches the user the token belongs to. Look at SPF and DKIM results from the provider and drop failures.
- Strip quoted replies and signatures so only the new text is saved.
- Accept attachments up to [10 MB], check type and size, and store them like other uploads.
- Process in a background job. Return 200 quickly.
- Ignore auto-replies and bounce messages (Auto-Submitted header, empty return path) to avoid mail loops.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Replying to a notification adds the reply text, without the quoted history, to the right thread.
2. An email from a different sender to the same reply address is rejected.
3. An out-of-office reply doesn't create anything or trigger another email.
4. The same webhook delivered twice creates one record.
5. A 50 MB attachment is refused cleanly.
acceptance_checks: Replying to a notification adds the reply text, without the quoted history, to the right thread.
An email from a different sender to the same reply address is rejected.
An out-of-office reply doesn't create anything or trigger another email.
The same webhook delivered twice creates one record.
A 50 MB attachment is refused cleanly.
if_you_skip_it: Anyone who learns an address can post into a user's account, or two auto-responders email each other forever.
